// diagnostic

E0777

A function uses an expert effect, such as `Meta.Code.Rewrite`, that its package doesn't hold

What

A function uses an expert effect, such as `Meta.Code.Rewrite`, that its package doesn't hold

Why

No package holds an expert effect by default, and holding a parent such as `Meta` never covers one: only the main package holds one, by naming it or an expert effect above it in `authority.allow`, and a dependency holds one only through the main package's `authority.grants` line for it; a `deny` row always wins

Fix

Add the effect to the main package's `authority: { allow: [...] }` row, or for a dependency to the main package's `authority: { grants: { "name": [...] } }` line, or stop using it

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0777: Tests/UI/MetaExpertLeafRootOnlyDependencyRaw/stderr.

Error [jet.ExpertEffectNotHeld]: `shapes` needs `Meta.Code.Raw`: `install` uses it, and the main package doesn't grant it
  --> shapes/shapes.jet:1:36
    |
  1 | install: fn(meta: Compiler) { meta.add("Shape: struct {{\n    id: I64,\n}}\n", scope: "shape") }
    |                                    ^^^
 Why: Only the main package holds an expert effect; a dependency uses one only where the main package lends it with `authority.grants`
 Fix: Add `authority: { grants: { "shapes": [Meta.Code.Raw] } }` to the main package's manifest, or stop using `Meta.Code.Raw` in `install`
 Denial: expert
 Call chain: install
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0777

Error [jet.DependencyCheckFailed]: Dependency package `shapes` has errors
 Why: A dependency package is checked as its own package; its errors, shown above, fail every package that imports it
 Fix: Fix the errors shown above; `jet check shapes` checks that package on its own
